# Proposal: Upgrade Compound Protocol to v3

## Summary
This proposal aims to upgrade the Compound protocol to version 3, introducing new features including:
- Multi-collateral support
- Improved liquidation mechanisms
- Gas optimization for transactions

## Motivation
The current v2 protocol has served the community well, but market demands require enhanced functionality.

## Specification
- Deploy new Comptroller contract at: 0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678
- Migrate existing markets to new architecture
- Implement 7-day timelock for security

## Voting Options
- For: Approve the upgrade
- Against: Reject the upgrade
- Abstain: No preference
forum_discussion: Simple SummaryFollowing Ethereum supply cap proposal, Gauntlet now extends the same risk-off methodology to Compound v3 deployments across seven L2 networks : Arbitrum, Base, Linea, Mantle, Optimism, Polygon, and Unichain , covering 16 Comets and 37 collateral assets. Under the same three-rule framework: 9 assets with negligible demand are being set to a cap of 0, and 28 active collateral assets are being resized to ~20–30% above current supply balances. Key collateral assets (WBTC, WETH, cbBTC, cbETH, USDC, USDT, wstETH) remain unaffected.BackgroundThis proposal is the L2 version toGauntlet’s Ethereum Supply Cap Recommendations, and operationalizes the same stance: given the elevated frequency of exploits and targeting long-tail collaterals across DeFi, supply-cap headroom that is not matched by organic demand is not “spare capacity” , it is unused risk surface. Compressing that headroom across the L2 footprint is the most direct action available without disrupting existing users.The L2 Comets carry a heterogeneous mix of LSTs, LRTs, network-native governance tokens (ARB, OP, WPOL, MaticX, GMX, UNI), wrapped BTC derivatives, and yield-bearing stablecoins (sUSDS, sFRAX). Demand is concentrated in a minority of listings per Comet; the remainder hold near-zero supply. This proposal aligns caps with where user demand actually sits today.MethodologyThe same three rules from the Ethereum proposal are applied uniformly across every L2 collateral in scope:Rule 1 - Dormant assets → cap to 0.Any collateral withless than 1% supply utilizationis reduced to a cap of 0. Existing positions remain fully functional (withdraw, repay, liquidate); only new incremental deposits are paused.Rule 2 - Active collateral assets → tight buffer.Caps are resized to sit~20–30% above current supply balance, preserving headroom for existing users to top up during volatility while sharply reducing uncovered exposure.Rule 3 - Key collateral assets (WBTC, WETH, cbBTC, cbETH, USDC, USDT) → no change.Not in scope for this proposal.An aggregate view:BucketAssetsActionRule 1: Utilization < 1%9Cap → 0Rule 2: Active collateral assets28Cap resized to ~20–30% above supplyRule 3: Key collateral assets—UnchangedAggregate Impact by ChainChainCometsCollaterals in ScopeArbitrum415Base35Linea12Mantle12Optimism35Polygon24Unichain24Detailed RecommendationsArbitrumArbitrum USDC CometSymbolCurrent CapSupply BalanceUtilizationProposed CapRuletETH5000.26%0Rule 1tBTC4013.23%0Rule 1 (see note)ezETH1,400785.59%102Rule 2 (~31% buffer)GMX120,0001,9971.66%2,596Rule 2 (~30% buffer)ARB16,000,0001,497,5659.36%1,946,834Rule 2 (~30% buffer)Note on tBTC:Utilization is nominally above the 1% threshold, but the absolute supply balance is 1 tBTC.
